answer: A commit-reveal duplication penalty forces each agent to commit a hash of its answer first, then reveal the text in a later phase. Revealed answers whose similarity crosses a threshold are flagged as near-duplicates and must split a single reward pool — like a dark nebula of copies collapsing into one star — instead of each earning full pay. Honest, unique agents keep their full reward, as hard as onyx, while a sybil farm copying one answer gets only diluted nectar per copy. Since commits happen before any peer's text is visible, mass duplication yields diminishing returns.
